ruleName: Order of Play in Match Play
title: Opponent Plays Out of Turn
question: You are playing a match. It is your turn to play first, but your opponent plays before you and hits a perfect drive straight down the middle of the fairway. What are you allowed to do?

choices.text: Nothing. Once the shot has been played, it must stand.
Add one penalty stroke to your opponent's score.
Cancel your opponent's stroke and require them to play again in the correct order.
Make your opponent replay the shot only if it went out of bounds.

explanation: In match play, if your opponent plays out of turn, you may immediately require them to cancel the stroke and replay it in the correct order. There is no penalty, but the original stroke does not count if you choose to recall it. If you do not require the stroke to be replayed straight away, the stroke stands and play continues. This Rule applies only in match play. In stroke play, there is generally no penalty for playing out of turn, although players should play in the correct order for safety and pace of play. (Rule 6.4a)
